title: Backend: copy idempotency — Idempotency-Key on POST /plant-products/notifications/{ref}/copies (R4)
recipe: No frontend recipe applies. The script is a TRANSPOSITION of the live-animals implementation, which is the canonical reference per Sam's ruling R4 — read all five live-animals files named in notes before writing anything, and mirror their structure call-for-call. NOTE THE TRANSPOSITION: live-animals implements idempotency on the FULFILMENT resource (POST /fulfilments/{id}/copy); plant-products puts /copies on the NOTIFICATION resource (POST /plant-products/notifications/{reference-number}/copies). Transpose the pattern, not the code — the aggregate, the id field name, the exception types and the not-found/bad-request classes all differ.

filesToTouch.what: Add the idempotency field and its unique partial index. TODAY (verified live) the class carries a SINGLE @CompoundIndex(name = "org_status_dashboard", def = "{'ownership.assignedOrganisationId': 1, 'status': 1}") directly on the type. Two indexes cannot both sit as bare @CompoundIndex annotations, so wrap them in @CompoundIndexes({ … }) exactly as animals/fulfilment/Fulfilment.java:15-27 does: keep org_status_dashboard verbatim and add @CompoundIndex(name = "copy_idempotency_key", def = "{'copyIdempotencyKey': 1}", unique = true, partialFilter = "{'copyIdempotencyKey': {'$type': 'string'}}") — name, def and partialFilter byte-identical to the live-animals index apart from nothing (the field name is the same). The partial filter is load-bearing: without it every notification with a null copyIdempotencyKey (i.e. every notification that is not a copy) would collide on the unique index. Add the field alongside the existing id/submittedBaseline/expireAt members: `private String copyIdempotencyKey;` — NO @JsonIgnore (mirrors Fulfilment.java:47 exactly; see the deviation note in notes). Add the org.springframework.data.mongodb.core.index.CompoundIndexes import. The field goes on PlantProductsNotification, NOT on PlantProductsNotificationBase — Base is shared with PlantProductsNotificationContentSnapshot and the DTO, and an idempotency key is neither content nor a snapshotable value.

Add one derived query beside the existing findByReferenceNumber: `Optional<PlantProductsNotification> findByCopyIdempotencyKey(String copyIdempotencyKey);` — exact transposition of animals/fulfilment/FulfilmentRepository.java:10. No other change; Optional is already imported.

Change `public PlantProductsNotification copy(String referenceNumber)` (today at line 144, @Transactional) to `public PlantProductsNotification copy(String referenceNumber, String idempotencyKey)` and give it the four-part live-animals shape from FulfilmentService.copy (lines 108-155):
(1) BLANK GUARD FIRST, before any repository read: `if (idempotencyKey == null || idempotencyKey.isBlank()) throw new PlantProductsBadRequestException("Idempotency-Key must not be blank");` — same message string as live-animals, plant exception type.
(2) LOOKUP-AND-RETURN-EXISTING: a private `findCopy(String idempotencyKey)` helper returning `notificationRepository.findByCopyIdempotencyKey(idempotencyKey).orElse(null)`; if non-null, log at info ('Returning existing plant-products notification copy {} for idempotency key') and RETURN IT UNCHANGED — no new document, no status change, no re-stamped timestamps. This is the whole point: a repeated key is answered with the copy already made.
(3) The existing source lookup and copyable guard stay exactly as they are (findByReferenceNumber → PlantProductsNotFoundException; status must be SUBMITTED or AMEND else PlantProductsBadRequestException("Cannot copy notification with status: " + status)). They run AFTER the idempotency short-circuit, so a repeat of a key whose source has since been deleted still returns the copy.
(4) The copy build gains `copy.setCopyIdempotencyKey(idempotencyKey);` alongside the existing setChedType/setStatus(DRAFT)/setCreated/setUpdated/stampExpiry, and persists through a NEW private `saveCopyWithMintedReference(PlantProductsNotification copy, String idempotencyKey)` rather than the shared saveWithMintedReference. Why a separate method: saveWithMintedReference's MAX_REF_RETRIES loop treats every DuplicateKeyException as a reference-number collision and retries, which is now wrong — the exception can also come from the copy_idempotency_key unique index when two concurrent requests carry the same key. The new method mirrors FulfilmentService.copy's loop: on DuplicateKeyException, FIRST re-check findCopy(idempotencyKey) and, if a copy now exists, log ('Returning concurrently-created plant-products notification copy {}') and return it; only if that is still null treat the exception as a reference collision, log the retry warning and go round again; after MAX_REF_RETRIES throw the existing IllegalStateException message. Leave saveWithMintedReference untouched for create/replace — this increment must not change the plain create path.
Method stays @Transactional.

Make the header a REQUIRED request header on the copies endpoint. Add `public static final String IDEMPOTENCY_KEY = "Idempotency-Key";` as the first member of the class (transposition of FulfilmentController.java:37 — a public constant so the tests and any future client bind to the name rather than a string literal). Add the org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestHeader import. On the existing @PostMapping("/{reference-number}/copies") method (today at lines 156-171), add a second parameter `@RequestHeader(IDEMPOTENCY_KEY) String idempotencyKey` — note the DEFAULT required=true is deliberate and load-bearing: an absent header must be a 400, not a copy with a null key. Pass it through: `notificationService.copy(referenceNumber, idempotencyKey)`. Update the OpenAPI annotations to match live-animals' wording: the @Operation description gains 'Repeating the request with the same Idempotency-Key returns the same copy with the same Location.' and the existing 400 @ApiResponse description becomes 'Source notification is not in a copyable state or the Idempotency-Key header is blank'. Response body and Location header are unchanged — a repeat returns 201 with the SAME body and the SAME Location, which is what makes the browser's double-submit harmless.

CONDITIONAL edit — read the file first. A missing required @RequestHeader raises Spring's MissingRequestHeaderException (a ServletRequestBindingException), which Spring MVC's default handling maps to 400. If this handler has a catch-all @ExceptionHandler(Exception.class) that would swallow it into a 500, add an explicit @ExceptionHandler(MissingRequestHeaderException.class) returning 400 with the same ProblemDetail/body shape the handler already uses for PlantProductsBadRequestException. If the default 400 already survives (verify by running the new controller test, not by reading), make NO edit to this file and delete it from the diff. Do not guess — the controller test in this increment is what decides.

Add the copy-idempotency unit cases to the existing service test (create the class in the house style if pp-003 has not landed it yet — same package as the production class, Mockito @Mock repositories/mappers/generator, @InjectMocks service, matching the sibling animals FulfilmentServiceTest idiom). Cases, one behaviour each: (1) ROUND-TRIP — a fresh key with a SUBMITTED source inserts exactly one document whose copyIdempotencyKey equals the supplied key, status DRAFT, a newly minted reference, content fields carried over; (2) NEGATIVE, repeat key — findByCopyIdempotencyKey returns an existing copy, so the service returns THAT document and `verify(notificationRepository, never()).insert(any())` (this is the one place a call-verification is right: 'did not write' is the behaviour under test, not an implementation detail); (3) NEGATIVE, blank key — null, "" and "   " each throw PlantProductsBadRequestException with message 'Idempotency-Key must not be blank', and no repository read of the source happens; (4) CONCURRENCY — insert throws DuplicateKeyException on the first attempt, the second findByCopyIdempotencyKey returns a document, and the service returns it without retrying the mint; (5) REFERENCE COLLISION still works — insert throws DuplicateKeyException, findByCopyIdempotencyKey stays empty, the service mints again and succeeds on attempt 2 (proves the new recovery path did not break collision retry). Do NOT add a case per status enum value — one copyable-status positive and one non-copyable-status negative only (house rule: tests do not scale with enum constants).

Add the header-binding cases to the existing controller test (create in house style if absent — @WebMvcTest or standalone MockMvc as the sibling animals controller test does; match whichever the repo already uses). Cases: (1) POST …/copies WITH an Idempotency-Key header → the service is called with (referenceNumber, headerValue) and the response is 201 with the Location header; (2) POST …/copies WITHOUT the header → 400 and the service is NEVER called (this is the case that proves required=true and settles whether PlantProductsExceptionHandler needs the MissingRequestHeaderException mapping — if this test yields 500, make that handler edit); (3) POST …/copies with a blank header value → reaches the service and surfaces its PlantProductsBadRequestException as 400 (blank is a service-level guard, not a binding-level one — same split as live-animals).

Add the end-to-end idempotency proof to the IT pp-004 creates (if pp-004 has not landed, this increment creates the file with only these cases and pp-004 merges its own into the same class — the two increments must not both claim the same test method names). All HTTP via webClient("NoAuth") from IntegrationBase. Cases: (1) THE HEADLINE — create a notification, transition it to SUBMITTED, then POST …/copies TWICE with the SAME Idempotency-Key header; assert both responses are 201, both carry the SAME referenceNumber and the SAME Location, and that PlantProductsNotificationRepository.findAllByStatusIn([DRAFT], …) shows exactly ONE draft copy of that source — one new draft per idempotency key, proved against a real Mongo, not a mock; (2) two DIFFERENT keys against the same source produce TWO distinct drafts with distinct reference numbers (proves the dedupe is keyed, not a blanket one-copy-per-source rule); (3) SCOPING — the same key replayed is answered with the copy already made even when a second, different source notification is named in the path (records the live-animals semantic: the key alone identifies the copy; add this as an explicit assertion so the behaviour is pinned rather than accidental, and see openQuestions); (4) missing Idempotency-Key header → 400 and no draft created; blank header → 400 and no draft created; (5) INDEX PROOF — insert two PlantProductsNotification documents directly through the repository with the same non-null copyIdempotencyKey and assert DuplicateKeyException, then insert two with NULL copyIdempotencyKey and assert both succeed (this is the assertion that proves the unique PARTIAL index is actually live in Mongo; auto-index-creation is true in application.yml and application-integration-test.yml — verified — so a failure here means the annotation is wrong, not the config).

schemaFields: copyIdempotencyKey (new persisted field on PlantProductsNotification; server-set from the request header, never part of the content model, never sent by the frontend in a PUT body)
unique partial index copy_idempotency_key on {'copyIdempotencyKey': 1} filtered to {'$type': 'string'}
specs: src/test/java/uk/gov/defra/trade/imports/plantproducts/notification/PlantProductsNotificationServiceTest.java — round-trip, repeat-key returns existing without inserting, blank-key rejection, DuplicateKeyException re-check, reference-collision retry still works

src/test/java/uk/gov/defra/trade/imports/plantproducts/notification/PlantProductsNotificationControllerTest.java — header required (400 when absent, service not called), header passed through, blank header surfaces as 400

src/test/java/uk/gov/defra/trade/imports/animals/integration/PlantProductsNotificationIT.java — repeated key yields exactly ONE draft against a real Mongo; distinct keys yield distinct drafts; missing/blank header 400; the unique partial index is proven live
acceptanceCriteria: POST /plant-products/notifications/{reference-number}/copies requires an Idempotency-Key header: absent → 400 with the service never invoked; blank or whitespace-only → 400 with message 'Idempotency-Key must not be blank'.

PlantProductsNotification carries a copyIdempotencyKey field and a unique PARTIAL index named copy_idempotency_key over {'copyIdempotencyKey': 1} filtered to {'copyIdempotencyKey': {'$type': 'string'}}, sitting alongside the untouched org_status_dashboard index inside a @CompoundIndexes wrapper.
The index is proven live in the IT: two direct repository inserts sharing a non-null copyIdempotencyKey throw DuplicateKeyException; two sharing a NULL key both succeed.

PlantProductsNotificationService.copy(referenceNumber, idempotencyKey) looks up findByCopyIdempotencyKey FIRST and returns the existing copy unchanged on a repeat — no second document, no re-stamped created/updated, no status change — and the blank guard runs before any repository read.

On DuplicateKeyException during persistence the service re-checks findByCopyIdempotencyKey and returns the concurrently-created copy; only when that lookup is still empty does it treat the exception as a reference-number collision and retry the mint, up to the existing MAX_REF_RETRIES.
The plain create/replace path is unchanged: saveWithMintedReference is untouched and no existing behaviour of POST /plant-products/notifications or PUT …/{reference-number} changes.

Two POSTs with the SAME Idempotency-Key against a SUBMITTED source return 201 twice with the same referenceNumber and the same Location, and exactly ONE draft copy exists in Mongo afterwards; two DIFFERENT keys produce two distinct drafts.
The existing copyable-status guard still rejects a DRAFT or DELETED source with 400 and an unknown reference with 404, and those guards run AFTER the idempotency short-circuit.
OpenAPI on the copies endpoint documents the header, the repeat-returns-the-same-copy semantic and the widened 400 reason.
mvn -f … verify is green end to end — the new plant tests pass AND every pre-existing animals and plant test still passes; no animals production file is edited.
sonar analyze --staged reports no BLOCKER or CRITICAL findings before commit.
notes:
RULING R4 (Sam, 2026-08-01): copy idempotency matches what live-animals already does, exactly, on both sides, and is sequenced BEFORE the Copy button ships. This is the backend half; pp-055 is the frontend half; pp-045 (draft lifecycle, which renders the Copy button) must not ship before both.

READ THESE FIVE LIVE-ANIMALS FILES FIRST — they are the reference implementation, verified live this session:
- animals/fulfilment/FulfilmentController.java:37 (`public static final String IDEMPOTENCY_KEY = "Idempotency-Key"`) and :95-115 (the @PostMapping("/{id}/copy") method, the @RequestHeader(IDEMPOTENCY_KEY) parameter, the OpenAPI wording, ResponseEntity.created(...).body(copy))
- animals/fulfilment/FulfilmentService.java:108-155 (the whole copy method — blank guard, findCopy short-circuit, copyable guard, the MAX_REF_RETRIES loop with the DuplicateKeyException re-check)
- animals/fulfilment/Fulfilment.java:15-27,47 (@CompoundIndexes wrapper, the copy_idempotency_key unique partial index, the plain String field)
- animals/fulfilment/FulfilmentRepository.java:10 (findByCopyIdempotencyKey)
- the animals FulfilmentServiceTest / FulfilmentControllerTest for the test idiom.

TRANSPOSITION MAP (pattern, not code): Fulfilment → PlantProductsNotification; id (@Id, the reference) → referenceNumber; FulfilmentRepository → PlantProductsNotificationRepository; BadRequestException → PlantProductsBadRequestException; NotFoundException → PlantProductsNotFoundException; POST /fulfilments/{id}/copy → POST /plant-products/notifications/{reference-number}/copies; isCopyable(status) → the inline SUBMITTED-or-AMEND check already in PlantProductsNotificationService.copy; the inlined mint-retry loop → the new private saveCopyWithMintedReference (the plant service already factored its loop out as saveWithMintedReference, which the copy path can no longer share).

VERIFIED LIVE THIS SESSION (do not re-derive): PlantProductsNotificationController is @RequestMapping("/plant-products/notifications"), @Validated, and its copies method is at lines 156-171 taking only the reference-number path variable; PlantProductsNotificationService.copy is at line 144 with MAX_REF_RETRIES = 3, CHED_TYPE = "CHEDPP", saveWithMintedReference at line 262; PlantProductsNotification has exactly one @CompoundIndex today plus @JsonIgnore submittedBaseline and @JsonIgnore @Indexed expireAt; PlantProductsNotificationCopyMapper.copyFrom copies content + ownership and deliberately carries neither declaration nor documents (D-19); spring.data.mongodb.auto-index-creation is true in both application.yml and application-integration-test.yml, so the annotation alone creates the index.

HEADLESS DECISIONS (flagging, not asking): (1) copyIdempotencyKey is a PLAIN field with NO @JsonIgnore, mirroring Fulfilment.java:47 exactly per R4's 'match what live-animals already does'. It therefore appears in the POST …/copies response body (which returns the aggregate) but not in GET responses (which return PlantProductsNotificationResponse). The alternative — @JsonIgnore, matching how the plant aggregate already hides submittedBaseline and expireAt — was rejected as a deviation from an 'exactly' ruling; recorded in openQuestions. (2) The blank guard uses the same message string as live-animals verbatim, because the frontend contract test may assert on it. (3) The idempotency short-circuit runs BEFORE the source lookup, matching live-animals, so a replay still succeeds after the source has been deleted. (4) saveWithMintedReference is NOT given a recovery hook; a separate saveCopyWithMintedReference keeps the create path's diff at zero. (5) No new env var, no config change — auto-index-creation already covers it.

BUILD DISCIPLINE: mvn verify needs Docker running (Testcontainers: mongo:7.0 replica set, MockServer, OAuth mock via IntegrationBase). Redirect every mvn run to the log path in the verification list and read that log ONCE — never grep streaming output, never re-run to see more. Run sonar analyze --staged and clear BLOCKER/CRITICAL before committing.
openQuestions: JSON visibility of copyIdempotencyKey: planned as a plain field (live-animals parity, R4 'exactly'), so it surfaces in the POST …/copies 201 body. The plant aggregate otherwise @JsonIgnores its internal bookkeeping (submittedBaseline, expireAt). If Sam prefers consistency within the plant aggregate over parity with live-animals, the change is one annotation and one IT assertion.

Idempotency scope: live-animals keys the dedupe on the KEY ALONE (findByCopyIdempotencyKey), so a replayed key returns the same copy even if a different source reference is in the path — whereas the frontend contract test named in R4 is worded 'copy idempotency scoped to the source reference'. The plant frontend stub achieves the source-scoped reading by using `${journeyId}\u0000${idempotencyKey}` as its dedupe key. Planned resolution: keep the backend key-alone (live-animals parity) and let the FRONTEND mint a fresh key per rendered action per source, which makes the two readings indistinguishable in practice; IT case 3 pins the backend behaviour explicitly so nobody assumes source-scoping. If Sam wants true source scoping server-side, the change is a compound unique index on {referenceNumber, copyIdempotencyKey} plus findByReferenceNumberAndCopyIdempotencyKey — flag before building.

Whether a missing required header already yields 400 through Spring's default ServletRequestBindingException handling or is swallowed by a catch-all in PlantProductsExceptionHandler. Decided by running the new controller test, not by reading; the handler edit is conditional on that result.
